title: Question 1
statement_text: Can the upper bound $\operatorname{utw}(\mathcal{G}_{X})\le 2^{\operatorname{td}(X)+1}-4$ be improved? In particular, is $\operatorname{utw}(\mathcal{G}_{X})$ at most a polynomial function of $\operatorname{td}(X)$?
context_text: The strong product $G_1\boxtimes G_2$ has vertex set $V(G_1)\times V(G_2)$, with $(v,x)(w,y)$ an edge if $v=w$ and $xy\in E(G_2)$, or $x=y$ and $vw\in E(G_1)$, or $vw\in E(G_1)$ and $xy\in E(G_2)$; thus $H\boxtimes K_c$ is $H$ with each vertex blown up into a clique $K_c$. The treedepth $\mathrm{td}(X)$ of a graph $X$ is the minimum height (number of vertices on a root-to-leaf path) of a rooted forest $F$ on $V(X)$ such that every edge of $X$ joins a vertex to one of its ancestors in $F$; arbitrarily large graphs can have bounded treedepth. $\mathcal{G}_X$ is the class of $X$-minor-free graphs, and the underlying treewidth $\mathrm{utw}(\mathcal{G})$ of a graph class $\mathcal{G}$ (Campbell et al.) is the least integer $k$ such that, for some function $f$, every $G\in\mathcal{G}$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $H\boxtimes K_{f(\mathrm{tw}(G))}$ for some graph $H$ of treewidth at most $k$. The authors prove that for every graph $X$ there is $c$ such that every $X$-minor-free graph $G$ with $\mathrm{tw}(G)<t$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $H\boxtimes K_{ct}$ for some $H$ of treewidth at most $2^{\mathrm{td}(X)+1}-4$; together with a lower-bound construction this gives $\mathrm{td}(X)-2\le\mathrm{utw}(\mathcal{G}_X)\le2^{\mathrm{td}(X)+1}-4$, so underlying treewidth and treedepth of the excluded minor are tied. Combined with the Grid-Minor Theorem, for planar $X$ every $X$-minor-free graph is a subgraph of $H\boxtimes K_c$ with $\mathrm{tw}(H)\le2^{\mathrm{td}(X)+1}-4$. Earlier, Campbell et al. showed $\mathrm{utw}(\mathcal{G}_{K_t})=t-2$ and $\mathrm{utw}(\mathcal{G}_{K_{s,t}})=s$ for $t\ge\max\{s,3\}$. The question asks whether the exponential gap between the lower and upper bounds can be closed.

title: Question 2
statement_text: Is there a function $f$ such that for every graph $X$ there exists a function $c$ such that for every positive integer $t$ and for every graph $G$ with $\operatorname{tw}(G)<t$ that does not contain $X$ as a topological minor, there exists a graph $H$ of treewidth at most $f(\operatorname{td}(X))$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $H\boxtimes K_{c(t)}$?
context_text: The strong product $G_1\boxtimes G_2$ has vertex set $V(G_1)\times V(G_2)$, with $(v,x)(w,y)$ an edge if $v=w$ and $xy\in E(G_2)$, or $x=y$ and $vw\in E(G_1)$, or $vw\in E(G_1)$ and $xy\in E(G_2)$; thus $H\boxtimes K_c$ is $H$ with each vertex blown up into a clique $K_c$. The treedepth $\mathrm{td}(X)$ of a graph $X$ is the minimum height (number of vertices on a root-to-leaf path) of a rooted forest $F$ on $V(X)$ such that every edge of $X$ joins a vertex to one of its ancestors in $F$; arbitrarily large graphs can have bounded treedepth. The authors prove the analogous statement for excluded minors: for every graph $X$ there is $c$ such that every $X$-minor-free graph $G$ with $\mathrm{tw}(G)<t$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $H\boxtimes K_{ct}$ with $\mathrm{tw}(H)\le2^{\mathrm{td}(X)+1}-4$, and they ask whether it extends to excluded topological minors. Campbell et al. showed that a monotone class has bounded underlying treewidth if and only if it excludes some fixed topological minor, and proved the weakening of this question with $\mathrm{tw}(H)\le f(\mathrm{td}(X))$ replaced by $\mathrm{tw}(H)\le|V(X)|$; this is tight for complete graphs (the underlying treewidth of $K_t$-topological-minor-free graphs is $t$ for $t\ge5$), which gives the question for complete $X$. They also proved it for $X=K_{s,t}$ with $s\le3$ (open for $s\ge4$), and that the underlying treewidth of $P_k$-free graphs is $\lfloor\log_2k\rfloor-1$, good evidence since $\mathrm{td}(P_k)=\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil$. A positive answer would also generalise the result that every graph of treewidth $t$ and maximum degree $\Delta$ is a subgraph of $T\boxtimes K_{24t\Delta}$ for a tree $T$ (the case $X=K_{1,\Delta+1}$).

title: Question 3
statement_text: Is there a function $g$ such that for every graph $X$, there is a constant $c$ such that for every $X$-minor-free graph $G$, $\chi_{p}(G)\leqslant c\cdot p^{g(\operatorname{td}(X))}$ for every $p\geqslant 1$?
context_text: For an integer $p\ge1$, a vertex colouring of $G$ is $p$-centered if every connected subgraph of $G$ either receives more than $p$ colours or contains a colour appearing exactly once in it; the $p$-centered chromatic number $\chi_p(G)$ is the least number of colours of such a colouring. Centered colourings characterize classes of bounded expansion and are central in parameterized algorithms on them; if $\mathrm{tw}(G)\le t$ then $\chi_p(G)\le\binom{p+t}{t}$, which is tight. The strong product $G_1\boxtimes G_2$ has vertex set $V(G_1)\times V(G_2)$, with $(v,x)(w,y)$ an edge if $v=w$ and $xy\in E(G_2)$, or $x=y$ and $vw\in E(G_1)$, or $vw\in E(G_1)$ and $xy\in E(G_2)$; thus $H\boxtimes K_c$ is $H$ with each vertex blown up into a clique $K_c$. The treedepth $\mathrm{td}(X)$ of a graph $X$ is the minimum height (number of vertices on a root-to-leaf path) of a rooted forest $F$ on $V(X)$ such that every edge of $X$ joins a vertex to one of its ancestors in $F$; arbitrarily large graphs can have bounded treedepth. The authors prove that for planar $X$ every $X$-minor-free graph is a subgraph of $H\boxtimes K_c$ with $\mathrm{tw}(H)\le2^{\mathrm{td}(X)+1}-4$ and $c=c(X)$, which gives $\chi_p(G)\le c\cdot p^{f(\mathrm{td}(X))}$; using a product structure with an extra path factor, they obtain the same for apex $X$ (graphs $X$ with a vertex $u$ such that $X-u$ is planar). They also prove an analogous bound for weak colouring numbers $\mathrm{wcol}_r$ for every excluded minor $X$, via chordal partitions, but cannot adapt this technique to $p$-centered colourings for arbitrary $X$, since they do not know how to use chordal partitions to build $p$-centered colourings.

title: Question 4
statement_text: Let $X$ be a graph. Let $f(X)$ be the infimum of all the real numbers $c$ such that there is a constant $a$, such that for every $X$-minor-free graph $G$ and every integer $r\geqslant 1$, $\operatorname{wcol}_{r}(G)\leqslant a\cdot r^{c}$. Theorem 3 and a construction of Grohe et al. [20] imply that $\operatorname{tw}(X)-1\leqslant f(X)\leqslant g(\operatorname{td}(X))$ for some function $g$. Is $f(X)$ tied to some natural graph parameter of $X$?
context_text: This question asks what graph parameter of the excluded graph $X$ determines the optimal polynomial exponent in the weak coloring number bound for $X$-minor-free graphs. The paper shows that neither treedepth, pathwidth, nor treewidth of $X$ alone determines this exponent.
